task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: minutes, initiations and same-position minutes as exposure
methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile gain most in the absent player's primary types, more often than chance or than a minutes/initiations baseline?
How should spells and cases be defined, and what is the effective independent sample (148 spells vs 11 cases)?
How can mechanical exposure (minutes and initiations) be separated from profile similarity?
How should the 'or' across four candidate predictors be handled to avoid multiplicity?

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (paired dD_A +0.1151, n=96 matched pairs; vs terminal +0.0777, n=25). [prior work] lists RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR and small-sample limits. It concerns team-level identity, not which teammate gains.

Opponent three-point luck has no persistent player component (split-half reliability 0.004). Shows that noisy per-player outcome measures can have near-zero reliability; [prior work] cites measure reliability and small-sample limits.

Swapping the primary initiator did not recover suppressed-play efficiency; swap-minus-same +0.039 (p=0.002, d=0.12), directionally worse, recorded as a powered null. Related to initiator replacement but not to absence-driven gainers.

No elite-creator gravity effect on teammate PPP at lags 1-3 (Jokic lag-1 ATT +0.0282, CI [-0.043,+0.099], n=1880); clean null on PPP, with a secondary distinct-initiator signal for Antetokounmpo noted as structure not efficiency.
Player and teammate sequential premiums are descriptive, limited by label/classification error and small cells (n ~30-70).
Star suppression by lineup/forced play type was described without placebo or matching; [prior work] notes later work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).
Descriptive BEST/AVOID tier table with player samples of 10-178 possessions and no outcome test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Descriptive ranking of cells without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading small-cell player/teammate sequence premiums as signal
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits: label or classification error and small sample; mechanism unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating per-player opponent 3-point outcomes as a persistent player trait
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as low measurement reliability (0.004) and small sample.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests which teammate absorbs an absent player's play types, or whether profile similarity predicts that teammate.
Related work records that absence of a connector shifts team-level offensive identity more than usage-matched controls ([prior work][prior work], supported, with a mechanical-floor risk).
Related work records that small-cell player-level play-type measures are noisy and sometimes artifacts ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work], FAM:[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer.
Whether minutes, initiations or same-position minutes predict the largest gainer better than profile similarity.
The effective number of independent absence cases, or the number of spells that satisfy a usable-exposure rule.
Any effect-size or base-rate for top-gainer identity.
own_inferences: The question has four candidate predictors joined by 'or', and teammates with more minutes or initiations have more opportunities to gain. A raw largest-gainer test is therefore probably dominated by exposure, and profile similarity is probably correlated with initiation volume.
If 148 spells come from only 11 absent players (cases), the effective independent sample is closer to 11, which gives low power to distinguish a hit rate from chance.
The top-1 hit rate under chance is about 1/k for a rotation of k eligible teammates, probably 1/7 to 1/9, so detecting a modest lift needs far more than 11 independent cases.
Largest gain selected by max is subject to regression to the mean and noise; per-spell gains on few absent-player-type possessions are unreliable.
uncertainties: Meaning of 'n=148', '148 spells' and '11 cases' is not defined: spells per case, and whether cases are players or player-seasons.
Definition of the absent player's 'primary types' and the pre-absence window is not specified.
Missing data on spell lengths, number of absent-type possessions per spell, and rotation sizes.
Retrieved records are only weakly relevant (scores about 0.07-0.10); there may be unretrieved prior absence work.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record addresses the question. Related records only reinforce known risks (mechanical floor, small samples, measurement reliability, artifact-prone descriptive rankings), which I would have flagged anyway. They support requiring baselines and clustering but did not change the decision.

blocking_constraints.text: If the 148 spells belong to 11 cases, the effective independent n is about 11, which cannot detect a modest lift in top-1 hit rate over chance (~1/8).
Per-spell counts of the absent player's primary-type possessions are likely small, making per-teammate gain estimates noisy and the max-gainer unstable.
Teammates with the most minutes or initiations can gain the most in raw counts by exposure alone, so raw largest-gainer cannot separate similarity from opportunity.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests who absorbs an absent player's play types. Only team-level identity displacement under connector absence ([prior work][prior work]) and general noise/artifact warnings were found, so the question is not answered by earlier work.

risks.text: Effective independent units may be 11 cases; spells within a case share the absent player, team, scheme and teammates, so inference must be clustered.

Opportunity (minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) mechanically drives raw gains and overlaps with the similarity predictors; gains must be normalised by exposure and compared against exposure baselines.
Four predictors joined by 'or' allow a flexible win; one primary predictor must be fixed with others secondary and corrected.
Largest gainer is a max statistic; teammates with low pre-absence usage in the types regress upward, and top-gainer identity is noisy.
Concurrent changes (replacement lineup, other absences, opponent, rest, trades, coaching changes, garbage time) alter who gains independently of profile similarity.
Few absent-type possessions per spell make per-teammate shares unreliable; a minimum possession and minutes rule is required.
Play-type and initiator labels derived from play-by-play are error-prone; profile similarity from a small pre-absence sample is itself noisy.
Top-1 hit rate must be compared with 1/k by rotation size, not 50%.
Primary types and profiles must be defined only from pre-absence games, not from games including absence.
Profile similarity must use only data before each spell, including for spells late in a season.

design.estimand: Primary: within spell, whether the teammate ranked most similar to the absent player on a pre-absence initiation-profile distance (e.g., Jensen-Shannon distance over play-type initiation shares, using pre-absence games only) is the teammate with the largest exposure-adjusted gain in the absent player's top-2 primary play types (change in per-100-team-possessions initiations of those types vs the teammate's own pre-absence rate). Estimand: top-1 hit rate minus its expectation under exposure-matched permutation within spell, plus rank-based (Spearman) association of similarity rank with gain rank. Minutes, initiation volume and same-position minutes are pre-specified comparator/secondary predictors, not co-primary.
design.unit: Absence spell (contiguous games missed by one rotation player), clustered by absent player (case); teammate as the within-spell alternative.
design.sample: Spells within the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data (regular season and playoffs) meeting pre-registered rules: absent player in the rotation before (e.g., >=20 mpg over >=20 prior games), spell >=3 games, >=K absent-type possessions in the pre window and in the absence window, teammates with >=M absence-window minutes. Report counts at each filter for spells (148) and cases (11) before any outcome is computed. Freeze with the 2025-26 playoffs data complete from 2026-06-21.
design.power: With 11 independent cases the test is effectively underpowered; before analysis, compute by simulation using the actual rotation sizes k per spell the minimum detectable hit-rate lift over the ~1/k chance rate at cluster-bootstrap level. If the minimum detectable lift is more than about 25 percentage points, label the primary test exploratory and report estimates with CIs without confirmatory claims. Do not treat the 148 spells as independent.
design.controls: Normalise gains by teammate exposure (absence-window minutes and baseline initiation rate). Include a baseline predictor (most minutes, most initiations, same-position minutes) and test whether similarity adds information beyond it (e.g., conditional logit of top-gainer with cluster-robust SEs). Exclude spells with overlapping absences of other key rotation players, trades or coaching changes; control for opponent strength, game state/garbage time, and playoff versus regular season. Use empirical-Bayes shrinkage on teammate gain rates to reduce regression-to-the-mean in the max statistic.
design.falsification: Placebo: assign each spell a random pseudo-absent player (same team, same season, similar minutes, games the player played) and repeat the analysis; similarity should not predict gain. Permutation of similarity ranks within spell. Split-half reliability of teammate gain rates (odd/even absence games) must be adequate, else the max-gainer is untrustworthy. Negative-control play types (not the absent player's primary types).
design.multiplicity: One primary test (similarity-based top-1 hit rate vs permutation). Three secondary predictors (minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) and sensitivity analyses reported with Holm correction; the 'or' reading of the hypothesis is not used to claim success.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the cluster-bootstrapped primary hit-rate lift over the permutation baseline has a 95% CI excluding 0, similarity adds information beyond the best exposure baseline in the conditional model, the placebo is null, and gain reliability is adequate. Rejected if the CI is within a pre-specified equivalence margin (e.g., +/-10 percentage points) with adequate power. Otherwise inconclusive; if min-possession filters leave fewer than ~20 independent cases, record as untestable at confirmatory standard.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play, rotation intervals and starters, plus derived play-type possession records, for 2022-23 through 2025-26 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13, playoffs complete from 2026-06-21); questions posed 2026-11-01. Freeze the file snapshot and graph-database build hash, and the label-derivation code version, before analysis.
